topics.topic: Whether execute_function must always read until channel closure or may stop early when the channel exceeds its bound
questions: Must execute_function always read until the channel closes, or must the first passage explicitly exempt the channel-over-bound case in which it stops reading early?

quotes: It MUST close its own copy of the channel's write end once bubblewrap has started, read the channel while the environment runs until it closes, and decode what it read with read_runner_report.
When the runner writes more it stops reading, kills the environment as for its wall deadline, decodes what it read and observes channel_over_bound, so the execution concludes resource_exhausted.
judgement.why: The first passage requires reading until closure, while the second requires stopping before closure when the channel exceeds its bound.
judgement.failure: a contradiction needs two quotes found verbatim in the texts

topics.topic: Whether and under what status, request-digest, and attempt-number conditions a requested approval counts after not_applied
questions: A requested approval cannot satisfy find_send_authority's definition of an approval that counts, which requires status approved; must operation_element_conclusion apply only the resend attempt-number cutoff to requested approvals, or must find_send_authority's counting rule include requested approvals?

No requested approval can count under find_send_authority because that function requires status approved; must the existing-approval check use only find_send_authority's resend attempt-number cutoff, or must requested approvals be added to what find_send_authority considers counting?

Must a post-not_applied requested approval count for the waiting conclusion, or does “counts” retain find_send_authority's requirement that the approval already be approved and have the matching request_digest?
How can a requested approval satisfy the instruction that it count according to find_send_authority when find_send_authority counts only approved approvals with the given request_digest?

After not_applied, must a requested approval with a different request_digest be ignored and replaced because it does not count under find_send_authority, or must the element wait on that existing requested approval despite the differing digest?

quotes: find_send_authority: [SECURITY_BOUNDARY] For a draft-write binding that is not a resend after not_applied MUST return ActivationAuthority with the store_position the RunContext carries in started_under; otherwise MUST return ApprovalAuthority for the oldest in store order of the element's approvals that count — for a resend after not_applied only those its behaviour note admits — read with ApprovalsOfElement, whose status is approved and whose request_digest equals the given request_digest; failing that, when the effect_class is state-transition or external-effect and the send is not a resend after not_applied, GrantAuthority for the active grant found with ActiveGrantOfNode for the run's pinned flow_version_id and the node; otherwise none. A destructive binding is never covered by a grant, and an approved approval whose request_digest differs is no authority and stays approved and unused.

operation_element_conclusion: [DETERMINISM_OR_ORDERING] Decides from the latest NodeExecution of the element, the one with the highest attempt_number, in this order: succeeded concludes succeeded with that record's outputs; outcome_unknown with its EffectAttempt applied concludes succeeded with no outputs when the binding has no output ports and otherwise failed with status outcome_unknown and detail applied_outputs_unknown; any status other than succeeded, service_unreachable and outcome_unknown concludes failed with that status and detail_code; then an approval of the element with status requested makes it wait with reason owner_approval and that approval_id — after an attempt resolved not_applied only one that counts for its resend (find_send_authority), whose attempt_number is greater than that attempt's; then outcome_unknown with its attempt unknown waits with reason outcome_unknown; then service_unreachable waits with reason service_unreachable; otherwise — no NodeExecution, or a latest outcome_unknown whose attempt the owner resolved not_applied — the element is not reached, so it is reached again when its node is next taken, and after not_applied its send needs a fresh approval (find_send_authority), which reach_operation_element requests (decision 32).

reach_operation_element: [BEHAVIOR] When find_send_authority returns None MUST, unless an approval of the element with status requested already exists — for a resend after not_applied only one that counts for it (find_send_authority), so a fresh approval is always requested after not_applied —, write one RequestApprovalChange for the element with the binding_id, input_digests, the prepared request_digest and an ApprovalPreview of the operation's service_id, operation_name and effect_class, the prepared request description and the element's input PortRefs; input_digests are the digests of every input value and file in input port name order, list elements in list order. Nothing is sent and the element waits with reason owner_approval for that approval, the existing requested one when there was one, even if its request_digest differs.
judgement.why: The resend notes require a requested approval to count by find_send_authority's rule, while that rule permits only approved approvals with a matching request_digest, making the prescribed waiting and existing-approval behavior impossible for a requested approval.
